subject: maths
question:
A pipe can fill a water tank in 36 minutes, and another can fill it in 48 minutes, but a third pipe can empty it in 18 minutes.

The first two pipes are kept open for 16 minutes at the beginning, and then the third pipe is also opened. How long does it take to empty the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total capacity of the tank be LCM(36, 48, 18) = 144 units.

Efficiency: A = +4 units/min, B = +3 units/min, C = −8 units/min.

Water filled by A and B in 16 minutes = 16 × (4 + 3) = 112 units.

Net efficiency when A, B and C are open = 4 + 3 − 8 = −1 unit/min.

Time required to empty the filled 112 units = 112 ÷ 1 = 112 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 112 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A to fill the tank = 36 minutes

Time taken by pipe B to fill the tank = 48 minutes

Time taken by pipe C to empty the tank = 18 minutes

Pipes A and B are kept open for 16 minutes initially.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Total Work is taken as the LCM of time taken by individual pipes.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = LCM of 36, 48 and 18 = 144 units

⇒ Volume filled by pipes A and B in 1 minute = 4 + 3 = 7 units

⇒ Volume filled by pipes A and B in 16 minutes = 7 × 16 = 112 units

⇒ After 16 minutes, pipe C is also opened.

⇒ Net efficiency of all three pipes A, B, and C = 4 + 3 − 8 = −1 unit/minute

⇒ A negative efficiency indicates that the tank will be emptied at a rate of 1 unit per minute.

⇒ Time taken to empty the 112 units already filled = 112 ÷ 1 = 112 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 112 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Principle

It operates on the exact same logic as Time & Work. The entire tank capacity acts as the Total Work.

Negative Efficiency (Leak or Outlet Pipe)

Inlet pipes add to the volume (+ efficiency), while outlet pipes or leaks remove volume (− efficiency). Net flow is the algebraic sum of all active pipes.

Filling vs. Emptying Conclusion

If the net efficiency is positive, the tank gets filled. If negative, whatever volume is currently present will get emptied over time.
